newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest hog prices seen dependent on weather.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest hog prices seen dependent on weather.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct hog price outlooks for Wednesday were mixed, depending on how much rain overnight moves into the Corn Belt, livestock dealers said.

"If it rains, prices could be lower, if not, they will be higher," one Illinois hog buyer said. Sources said if enough rain falls to make fields muddy, farmers will be forced to stay out of the fields and will have time to sell hogs.
"It all depends on how many hogs we get," the buyer said.
Two storms were seen spreading through the Midwest, with the first arriving Tuesday, which could halt fieldwork in much of Iowa, Illinois and Indiana, Weather Services Corp said.
Rain from the back-to-back systems could last into the weekend, WSC said.

Interior Iowa/southern Minnesota top prices for hogs delivered to plants on Tuesday was $59.00 per cwt. Illinois top price for hogs at the plant were $57.50 and the top price for Indiana/Ohio plant hogs were $58.50.
Even if marketings increase, firm pork demand could limit cash hog price declines, if pork demand continues strong, sources said.

The central U.S. carlot pork midday report by USDA said fresh loins sold steady to $2.00 per cwt higher. Skinned hams were also quoted steady to $2.00 higher and seedless bellies steady to $3.00 lower.
